dk-5z6w.title: Pole: ordinary street poles are rare
dk-5z6w.summary: Normal roadside utility poles are rare. Most power infrastructure is large towering pylons, often near highways.

dk-6bR5.title: Bollard: white, yellow reflector, orange stripe
dk-6bR5.summary: White bollard with a yellow reflector and a dark orange stripe, found nowhere else. A green version also exists.

differs.how: Belgian bollards look similar but never have the orange stripe

dk-95gK.title: Roofs: thick seaweed thatch
dk-95gK.summary: Traditional roofs made of eelgrass, a type of seaweed, are found on the island of Læsø.

dk-AQr9.title: Location: North Atlantic islands, autonomous
dk-AQr9.summary: The Faroe Islands are a group of islands in the North Atlantic, an autonomous territory of Denmark. See their own guide.

dk-Dfcn.title: Guardrail: square B-type, no reflectors
dk-Dfcn.summary: Square (normal B-type) guardrails with no reflectors. Very few European countries use this type.

dk-Expm.title: Post box: national postal company
dk-Expm.summary: The national postal company, PostNord (Post Danmark), uses distinctive post boxes.

dk-Fhf5.title: Bus: company by region, colour scheme
dk-Fhf5.summary: Six regions each have their own bus company, with its name on the front and its own colours.

dk-Hx8L.title: Road numbers: ordered east to west
dk-Hx8L.summary: Roads are numbered from east to west. Numbers starting 2 to 5 group by region. Roads starting with 1 are nationwide, but the second digit still follows a rough region, and Bornholm only has roads starting with 1.

dk-I8Xz.title: Plate: white, yellow, or 'parrot' yellow left part
dk-I8Xz.summary: Standard plates are long, white with a blue strip. Commercial plates are yellow. 'Parrot' plates have a yellow section on the left and are unique here.

differs.how: Dutch private cars use fully yellow plates
Luxembourg private cars use fully yellow plates
UK private cars use yellow rear plates

dk-MZX3.title: Houses: timber frame walls
dk-MZX3.summary: Some older or rural buildings have timber-frame walls. Common across western and central Europe, but especially for historic buildings here.

dk-N0Lu.title: Location: world's largest island, a Danish territory
dk-N0Lu.summary: Greenland is the world's largest island country and is part of Denmark. See its own guide.

dk-NemR.title: Bollard: stone, red top, near cycle paths
dk-NemR.summary: Rare stone bollards, sometimes painted red on top, found near bicycle paths.

dk-PUXX.title: Houses: red brick with orange, brown or black tiles
dk-PUXX.summary: A lot of red brick buildings with orange, dark brown or black tiled roofs. The Netherlands and Belgium look similar.

dk-PXr5.title: Sign: green bicycle signs
dk-PXr5.summary: Green bicycle route signs are found on the island of Bornholm.

dk-SVbg.title: Sign: low direction sign in a pipe frame
dk-SVbg.summary: Low, red and white or blue and white direction signs framed by pipes, with the arrow built into the background. Bigger signs have a normal layout, and highway signs are blue or green.

dk-TriN.title: Roadside: bicycle paths
dk-TriN.summary: Bicycle paths sometimes run beside the road. Common in the Netherlands and Belgium too.

dk-UVfB.title: Sign: town entry sign, red slash when leaving
dk-UVfB.summary: A distinctive sign when entering a town. On the way out the same sign has a red slash through it.

dk-Wd1V.title: Roads: ring roads O1 to O4
dk-Wd1V.summary: Special highways around bigger cities are labelled O1 to O4, with the number going up away from the centre. Cities with them: Copenhagen, Odense, Aarhus, Aalborg, Hillerød, Kolding, Vejle.

dk-X28G.title: Sign: pipe frame bent around the sign
dk-X28G.summary: A signpost where the pipe frame is bent around the sign. Unique to this country.

dk-bHDl.title: Chevron: red and white, low to the ground
dk-bHDl.summary: Red and white chevron signs, often set low to the ground.

dk-bVRk.title: Bus stop: green, red and white
dk-bVRk.summary: Bus stops on the island of Bornholm are green, red and white.

dk-cK6E.title: Sign: bus stop sign by region
dk-cK6E.summary: Each of those regions also has its own bus stop sign design.

dk-ctgh.title: Roofs: thatched, or grey corrugated
dk-ctgh.summary: Some houses, especially rural ones, have thatched roofs. Grey corrugated roofs also appear and look a bit like ones in the Baltic countries.

dk-dC2V.title: Landscape: flat, open fields between towns
dk-dC2V.summary: A flat country with wide open fields between towns. Suburbs are open with space between buildings, and town centres are denser.

dk-dYhG.title: Gas stations: four brands shared with neighbours
dk-dYhG.summary: Ingo is also in Sweden, OK in the Netherlands, and Uno-X and Yx in Norway.

dk-iepe.title: Road lines: all white, double centre lines
dk-iepe.summary: All road lines are white, and double centre lines are very common. Poland and Greece can have double lines too.

differs.how: can also have double centre lines
can also have double centre lines

dk-lm-24568.title: Landscape: long fjords, steep green mountains
dk-lm-24568.summary: Long wide fjords with jagged green mountains rising straight from the water and rocky ridges. They look more imposing and greener than Iceland's coastal mountains.

differs.how: Icelandic coastal mountains are less green and less imposing

dk-lm-2989.title: Sign: relaxed walking figure, rounded edges
dk-lm-2989.summary: The pedestrian figure walks in a relaxed way, with rounded edges and arms pointing down, often on a thick 3D blue square. Similar Scandinavian signs have different arms.

dk-lm-3316.title: Bus company: Bornholm transport
dk-lm-3316.summary: The Bornholm transport company buses and stops mark the island of Bornholm.

dk-lm-3317.title: Bus company: Midttrafik
dk-lm-3317.summary: Midttrafik is the bus company for central Jutland.

dk-lm-3330.title: Bus company: NT
dk-lm-3330.summary: NT is the transit company for northern Jutland.

dk-lm-3331.title: Bus company: Movia
dk-lm-3331.summary: Movia runs transit on Zealand, Lolland, Falster and Møn.

dk-lm-3332.title: Bus colour: green buses
dk-lm-3332.summary: Funen, Langeland and Ærø use green buses.

dk-lm-3358.title: Bus company: Sydtrafik
dk-lm-3358.summary: Sydtrafik is the transit company for mainland southern Jutland.

dk-mA1R.title: Language: Æ, Ø and Å letters
dk-mA1R.summary: A Scandinavian language using Æ, Ø and Å. Norwegian uses all three, Faroese has Æ and Ø, Icelandic only Æ, and Swedish Å plus Ä and Ö, which Danish lacks.

dk-mbZq.title: Google car: old Gen 2, gloomy sky, sandy roadside
dk-mbZq.summary: The small island of Anholt only has older Gen 2 coverage, with grey overcast weather and a lot of sandy dirt beside the road.

dk-o1S7.title: Road lines: edge line of small white squares
dk-o1S7.summary: Outer lines often look like a row of small white squares. A very good clue for the country.

dk-qCU5.title: Street sign: blue with white text, ends in 'vej'
dk-qCU5.summary: Most street names end in 'vej', the word for street. Street signs are mostly blue with white text.

dk-sRx7.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 5 stripes
dk-sRx7.summary: The pedestrian sign has 5 stripes, with the first and fifth touching the edge of the white triangle. Sweden has 4 stripes, and Norway almost always 4.

dk-ulal.title: Sign: black and yellow bus stop
dk-ulal.summary: Bus stop signs are black and yellow, with a small sign on top of the pole and the timetable below. An older blue and white version exists too.
